pair_convention.spot_explanation: NZD/USD 0.58818 means 1 NZD buys 0.58818 USD. A rising quote means the New Zealand dollar is strengthening against the US dollar (bullish for the pair, pair RISES); a falling quote means the New Zealand dollar is weakening against the US dollar (bearish for the pair, pair FALLS). All levels, targets and pip calculations in this report are anchored to this convention.

executive_summary: NZD/USD sits at 0.58818 on the gated price store's 3 September close, two sessions after the stated valuation date, and the pair has done almost nothing for six months: minus 0.10 per cent over one month, plus 1.25 per cent over three, minus 0.62 per cent over six and minus 1.80 per cent over twelve. That stasis has resolved twice inside the last three weeks and both times against the New Zealand dollar. Spot spiked to an intraday 0.59886 on 21 August — a marginal lower high against the 0.59937 of 29 May — and has fallen 107 pips since, including a 106-pip range on 2 September when the Reserve Bank delivered the 94 per cent priced increase to 2.75 per cent alongside an OCR track essentially unchanged from May. That is the central bilateral fact of this report: the base leg's only high-information repricing event has now fired and delivered nothing, while the quote leg's — a Federal Reserve decision with a full projection round on 16 September — is still ahead. The two standalone dossiers were both bullish their own currency, and the pair resolution is that one of those bullish cases has been tested and found wanting. The direction verdict is Bearish at conviction 3 on both horizons, net weighted scores of minus 0.3126 tactically and minus 0.3254 strategically, and the price payload corroborates rather than contradicts it: spot is 105 pips below a 200-week average it has not closed above for 28 weeks, the daily averages are stacked short-below-long inside a 20-pip tangle, and the pair's own 25-delta risk reversals are negative at every tenor and steepen monotonically from minus 0.193 per cent at 38.6 days to minus 0.617 at 185.7. The caveat is dated and specific: hike odds for 16 September fell to roughly 50 per cent from 63 per cent after Governor Waller signalled a preference for a hold, which erodes the single unpriced input the tactical case leans on, and a doubly crowded pair-short in a base-leg futures market of only 88,964 contracts can squeeze hard.

market_context.valuation_assessment: Neither dossier offers a pair-level PPP estimate. On REER relatives, the base currency's 101.12 against the quote's 107.84 for June 2026 implies NZD is roughly 6.2 per cent cheap to USD in real terms, mapping to a notional 0.6285 against spot of 0.58818 — a discount in place for twelve months without closing and materially smaller than the 12.8 per cent gap identified against AUD. This is a structural background condition, not a tactical signal: a real discount that has failed to close across four quarters of a hiking central bank will not close inside four weeks. The 61st closing percentile of the 52-week range describes a pair that is neither distressed nor extended, consistent with a 112.5bp negative carry, a policy rate seventh of ten in the G10, and a current account deficit of 3.6 per cent of GDP. The 52-week intraday range and percentile (3rd) are corrupted by a bad tick on 29 April 2026 and are not used.

market_context.recent_regime: The pair's regime over the last twenty-five sessions is a failed upside resolution. From a 0.57712 close on 23 July it climbed through a 30 July gap to 0.58797, chopped inside 0.5850-0.5901 for a fortnight, then surged 19-21 August to close 0.59795 with an intraday 0.59886 — the highest print since May — before failing at the four-touch resistance band. The subsequent seven sessions gave back 107 pips, including a 106-pip range on 2 September when the RBNZ delivered a widely expected hike alongside a dovish-read OCR track, followed by a 31-pip recovery on 3 September driven by the quote leg after Waller signalled a preference for a hold. The dominant narrative going into the tactical window is whether the Federal Reserve delivers on 16 September, not the base leg.

bilateral_carry_analysis.breakeven_move: At 94.9bp annualised on spot of 0.58818, carry accrues at 55.8 pips a year, or 4.7 pips a month. A long must appreciate that much simply to break even; a short earns it. Against ATR(14) of 47 pips, carry provides no meaningful cushion at either horizon and any position must be justified on direction alone, though the strategic short is paid to wait.
bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The gated rate block carries the policy differential at minus 112.5bp pre-decision, narrowing to minus 87.5bp after the 2 September RBNZ hike to 2.75%. Carry pays the short side of this pair. On the gated 3M implied volatility of 8.266%, the carry-to-vol ratio is a modest minus 0.106 to minus 0.136 — small in absolute terms, making negative carry a persistent drag on a long rather than a driver of direction; a single average 47-pip session erases roughly ten months of accrual. The tradable cost is better measured by the gated futures roll premium of plus 94.9bp annualised, which by covered interest parity embeds both the interest differential and the cross-currency basis (implying a basis of roughly minus 18 to minus 27bp, a derivation not a quote). This is a modest dollar funding premium rather than a stress signal, and it means the strategic short is paid to wait rather than penalised for waiting — materially different from the base dossier's preferred AUD/NZD expression only in magnitude, not in sign.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The gated payload carries the differential at minus 112.5 basis points against the New Zealand dollar, being an Official Cash Rate of 2.50 per cent as at 28 August against a federal funds midpoint of 3.625 per cent as at 1 September, with the ten-year differential at minus 1 basis point on two June monthly vintages that carry no live information. The base leg has since moved: the Reserve Bank delivered the 25 basis point increase to 2.75 per cent on 2 September by consensus, narrowing the policy gap to minus 87.5 basis points. That narrowing is not the tactically relevant fact, because the decision was priced at 94 per cent and the republished OCR track was little changed from May, with a fourth-quarter 2026 average of 2.81 per cent against 2.84 per cent in May, a profile consistent with a pause on 28 October and a 25 basis point increase to 3.00 per cent on 9 December. The base leg's only high-information repricing event inside the tactical window has therefore been resolved without surprise, while the quote leg's is still ahead: the Federal Reserve decides on 16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections attached and a hike priced at roughly 57 to 66 per cent in futures against roughly 48 to 55 per cent in prediction markets, leaving 34 to 43 percentage points of upside surprise available. The transmission is direct and mechanical — a Federal Reserve increase restores the differential to minus 112.5 basis points and widens the New Zealand two-year deficit of roughly 73 basis points toward 95 in a single session, against a New Zealand front end that has just been told to expect nothing until December.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the level and the direction of travel of this differential point in opposite directions with almost equal force, which is the honest basis for a Neutral rather than a hedge. On direction, the Reserve Bank is the only one of the two banks with a published tightening path still to run: the September track implies 3.00 per cent by the 9 December Statement, while the Federal Reserve's own June projections carry a 2026 median of 3.8 per cent and a 2027 median of 3.6 per cent, which makes any September increase terminal and the following move a reduction. If both banks deliver as their own guidance implies, the gap sits at roughly minus 87.5 basis points at the end of the window rather than minus 112.5, and it narrows further into 2027. On level, minus 87.5 basis points is still a material negative carry and the gated futures roll premium of 94.9 basis points annualised is what a rolled long position actually pays regardless of who is right about the path. Both banks also decide on the same two dates inside the window — 28 October and 9 December, with the RBNZ publishing a new track and the Federal Reserve a new SEP on 9 December — so the differential is repriced simultaneously rather than sequentially, which removes the usual first-mover advantage from either leg. Direction favours the pair modestly, level and carry oppose it, roughly 40 basis points of the convergence is already in the two-year spread, and the standoff is genuine.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral inflation differential is the reverse of what the headlines imply and that inversion is the core of this factor. New Zealand's headline is higher — 4.06 per cent on the cached OECD second-quarter vintage against 3.4 per cent United States CPI — but the measures the two central banks actually target point the other way: the Reserve Bank's sectoral factor model core has been pinned at 2.7 per cent for four consecutive quarters, inside the 1 to 3 per cent band, while United States core PCE has been stuck at 3.3 per cent for three months with headline PCE at 3.7 per cent and a six-month annualised rate of 4.1 per cent. The economy with the genuine underlying inflation problem is the quote economy, not the base economy. The growth and labour differentials compound in the same direction: United States GDP is 2.1 per cent year on year against New Zealand's 1.47 per cent, unemployment is 4.1 per cent against 5.6 per cent — a New Zealand decade high — and the Atlanta Fed nowcast for the third quarter stands at 4.8 per cent against New Zealand retail volumes falling 0.5 per cent in the June quarter and house prices 0.7 per cent lower on the year. The counterweight is real and is why confidence sits in the low fifties rather than higher: United States payrolls fell 23,000 in July with average hourly earnings at a five-year low of 3.2 per cent, and the RBNZ's September Statement raised its very near-term growth forecasts and said activity should strengthen and broaden. Transmission over four weeks runs through which economy's data forces its central bank's hand, and asymmetric sensitivity favours the quote leg: 4 September payrolls and 11 September CPI both land before the FOMC, whereas New Zealand's own quarterly data is 63 days stale and its next binding prints arrive after the Reserve Bank has already committed to a pause.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both inflation processes are level shifts that fade, and the question is which economy is left standing with the better growth and labour profile once they do. New Zealand's overshoot is imported: tradables inflation of 4.9 per cent rests on a 27.5 per cent petrol contribution and Brent has fallen roughly 12 per cent from its July high, while one-year inflation expectations collapsed 81 basis points to 2.60 per cent in the August survey. The United States overshoot is substantially tariff-driven at an average statutory rate of 11.0 per cent, which also drops out of year-on-year comparisons, and the inverted core PCE to core CPI wedge of 80 basis points is the signature of exactly that pass-through. So both disinflate, and the differential resolves on the real economy — where the base economy is materially weaker: private-sector ordinary-time wage growth of 2.0 per cent against 4.1 per cent inflation means real wages falling 2.1 per cent, services employment has been below 50 for thirty-two consecutive months, and house prices sit roughly 17 per cent below their November 2021 peak in the economy where housing is the dominant transmission channel. Confidence is cut from the base dossier's standalone reading because the RBNZ's September Statement explicitly revised 2027 inflation forecasts up on persistent domestic inflation, with a majority of the Committee seeing upside inflation risks — a direct challenge to the imported-and-fading thesis — while simultaneously moderating its medium-term growth forecasts and recording all members seeing downside risks to growth. That combination is bearish for the pair in a different way than the dossier argued: stickier New Zealand inflation supports the rates leg but the growth downgrade is the more currency-relevant half.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The sign convention for this pair is unusually clean: the base currency benefits from risk appetite and the quote currency benefits from its absence, so risk-on is pair-positive and risk-off is pair-negative with no ambiguity about which leg dominates. The current cross-asset reading is emphatically benign — the VIX closed at 14.43 on 28 August against 20.66 a month earlier, a fall of 6.23 points; United States investment-grade option-adjusted spreads are 79 basis points and high yield 260 to 263 basis points, both near cycle tights and high yield roughly 27 basis points tighter on the month; and the S&P 500 finished August at 7,686.14. In level terms that is a pair-positive configuration. What removes the directional signal is that the level is already at the boundary of its range in both instruments, so the distribution of outcomes from here is heavily one-sided: there is a few basis points of credit tightening available and several hundred of widening, and every basis point of widening hits the high-beta base leg twice, once through risk and once through dollar funding. The one genuinely two-sided tactical input is China, the base economy's largest export destination, where the official manufacturing PMI improved to 49.8 in August from 49.2 and beat a 49.7 consensus while the S&P Global RatingDog measure rose to 51.5 — an improvement from a weak base rather than a deterioration. Supportive levels against a hostile distribution, with an improving but sub-50 Chinese manufacturing print in the middle, is a Neutral rather than a hedge.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months a VIX of 14.43 and a high-yield spread of 260 basis points are levels to fade rather than extrapolate, and this pair has the worst convexity in the G10 to that fade. The mechanism is structural and specific rather than a generic risk-off argument. The base economy must import capital continuously to fund a current account deficit of 3.6 per cent of GDP against a net international investment position of minus 42.8 per cent and net external debt of 49.0 per cent, it is the least liquid major currency with documented gapping behaviour outside Australasian and London hours, and its central bank has no standing dollar swap line with the Federal Reserve where the Reserve Bank of Australia does. The quote leg is the other side of every one of those sentences. The demand channel adds to it: China printed second-quarter GDP of 4.3 per cent below its own 4.5 to 5 per cent target and has spent two months with official manufacturing below 50, and Chinese dairy buying was described as being at historic lows at the June auction with July whole milk powder exports to China down 12.8 per cent year on year — though the August PMI improvement and a RatingDog reading of 51.5 are genuine counterweights and are the reason confidence is only 53. The transmission is that any move toward wider credit and higher volatility is expressed in this pair with amplification, and the strategic edge is not a forecast of higher volatility but the observation that the pair retains all of the downside beta from a starting point that offers almost no further upside.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Positioning is the only factor pointing up for this pair and it does so because the two legs reinforce rather than offset. Leveraged funds were net short 31,994 New Zealand dollar contracts as at the 25 August report date, having added 5,188 on the week, against total open interest of only 88,964 contracts of NZD 100,000 — one of the two smallest currency futures markets in the G10 — while non-commercial length in the Dollar Index stood at 18,682 contracts, down for a fourth consecutive week from a 22,499 peak on 4 August described as around a three-and-a-half-year high. Specs are therefore short the base and long the quote, which amplifies the implied pair-short rather than muting it, and any covering is transmitted through the bilateral pairs because Dollar Index open interest is small. The gated payload adds the corroborating instrument the base dossier could not obtain: 25-delta risk reversals of minus 0.193 per cent at 38.6 days, minus 0.374 at 94.7 and minus 0.617 at 185.7, with butterflies rising from 0.142 to 0.242 — persistent and tenor-increasing demand for downside protection in this pair. Confidence is cut to 44 for two reasons. First, the trigger has passed: the squeeze case rested on a hawkish OCR track, and the 2 September Statement published a path little changed from May, so the base leg's covering catalyst delivered nothing. Second, the base-leg figures carry an unreconciled series conflict, with the legacy non-commercial series showing minus 14,200 for the same report date against the Traders in Financial Futures reading of minus 31,994, disagreeing on both level and the direction of the weekly change.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At a one-to-six-month horizon positioning carries almost no information in either leg and the honest answer is Neutral at low confidence. The base-leg book turns over faster than the window: the asset-manager category alone moved 25,889 contracts in a single week, equal to 29 per cent of total open interest, so whatever the book looks like now says nothing about February, and the current short of 31,994 contracts is not an extreme by this market's own history, the prior cycle having recorded minus 47,700 on the legacy basis at 31 July. The quote-leg book is also being reduced rather than accumulated, four consecutive weeks off a multi-year high, which means the medium-term distribution of change there is skewed toward further reduction — a mild pair-positive that offsets the base leg's mild pair-negative. The two structural flows that do survive the horizon point in opposite directions and roughly cancel. Against the pair: the dollar's share of allocated global reserves at 57.13 per cent is roughly fifteen percentage points below its 2001 peak, which is a slow pair-positive drag on the quote leg, but the latest quarter actually rose 0.71 percentage points from 56.42 per cent and the IMF has attributed the majority of past declines to valuation rather than active selling. For the pair: Japanese retail margin accounts are a significant unmeasured holder of New Zealand dollar carry exposure, but that exposure is expressed against the yen rather than the dollar and does not read across cleanly here. What is left is a genuine absence of durable information, and the tenor-steepening risk reversal skew is the only persistent signal — mildly bearish, not enough to move the stance.

Tactically a doubly crowded pair-short in a base-leg futures market of only 88,964 contracts is a real mechanical support. Strategically the same books turn over roughly monthly on both sides, the base-leg short is not at an extreme by its own history, and the quote-leg reduction offsets it, so the factor reverts to carrying no directional content.

tactical.combined_positioning_signal: Specs are short the base at 31,994 contracts and long the quote at 18,682 contracts, so the implied pair-short is crowded on both legs simultaneously — the amplified rather than the muted configuration, and the reason positioning is the only factor pointing up.
tactical.unwind_trigger: A Federal Reserve hold on 16 September against 57 to 66 per cent priced for a hike. That is now the only dated event inside the window capable of forcing covering on both legs at once, because the base leg's own trigger — a hawkish OCR track — was resolved on 2 September with a path little changed from May.

A short base that large failing to produce a rally is evidence that the selling was fundamental rather than speculative, and it is the strongest argument against the squeeze case.

The case for the crowd is that the differential remains negative at minus 87.5 basis points, the terms of trade are falling, and the gated risk reversals show downside protection being bid at every tenor rather than being sold into strength. The crowd is better funded and, now that the base-leg catalyst has passed without a hawkish surprise, better timed.

strategic.unwind_trigger: A Federal Reserve reduction inside the window against a Reserve Bank that reaches 3.00 per cent on 9 December, which would compress the differential toward minus 60 basis points and remove the carry rationale for holding the pair short.
strategic.historical_analogue: The quote leg offers the cleaner analogue: non-commercial length peaked at 22,499 contracts on 4 August and had already been cut 17 per cent before the most hawkish central-bank communication of the year, so the quote-leg book was lighter into its catalyst than the headline level implied — the reverse of the crowded-long-into-an-event setup that usually precedes a reversal.
strategic.contrarian_case: The genuine strategic contrarian risk to a bearish pair view is that a covered base-leg short removes the mechanical support that has quietly limited declines, so the pair enters the fourth quarter with a cleaner slate at the moment the external accounts stop improving — which argues the bearish case gets easier, not harder. The offsetting risk is that the quote leg's reserve share is fifteen percentage points below its 2001 peak and any dollar rally is a selling opportunity for real money, which caps how far the pair can fall on flow grounds alone.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both economies run external deficits, so the bilateral question is whose is deteriorating faster and whose is more expensive to finance. On the base side the tactical evidence is a single ugly print and two scheduled releases: the July merchandise trade balance came in at minus 1.95 billion New Zealand dollars against an expectation nearer minus 175 million, taking the annual balance from minus 3.75 to minus 5.24 billion in one month, and the June-quarter Overseas Trade Indexes plus the ANZ commodity index for August both landed on 3 September after a July commodity index fall of 3.9 per cent in world terms, its largest monthly decline since November 2022, with the dairy sub-index down 6.5 per cent on the month and 11.3 per cent on the year. On the quote side the advance goods trade balance printed minus 118.8 billion dollars against minus 100.8 expected, an 18 billion single-month deterioration, so the quote leg is not clean either — which is precisely why confidence is 53 rather than the base dossier's standalone 58. The bilateral trade relationship itself is immaterial as a flow driver: IMF Direction of Trade Statistics for 2024 put base exports to the quote economy at 5.5 billion dollars against imports of 4.9 billion, a net balance of 0.5 billion in the base economy's favour on roughly 10.4 billion of two-way goods trade, which is trivial against either economy and generates no structural currency demand in this pair. Transmission over four weeks therefore runs through commodity prices and scheduled data rather than through trade settlement, and it tilts against the pair because dairy has stopped falling without starting to pay — whole milk powder at 3,585 dollars a tonne after four consecutive positive auctions remains below its 3,706 dollar level of early June.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is the heaviest strategic factor at 0.16 and it is negative for the pair, but by a narrower margin than the base dossier alone implies because the quote economy's external position is also deteriorating in composition. The base economy runs a current account deficit of 3.6 per cent of GDP whose improvement stalled three quarters ago, on a primary income deficit of roughly 3.3 billion New Zealand dollars a quarter and a net international investment position of minus 42.8 per cent of GDP; terms of trade fell 2.0 per cent in the March quarter; dairy is roughly 30 per cent of merchandise exports with the ANZ sub-index down 11.3 per cent year on year and Fonterra having cut its 2026/27 farmgate forecast from a 9.75 to a 9.25 dollar midpoint on explicitly weaker reference prices. The quote economy's deficit is 2.9 per cent of GDP and widening, its net international investment position is minus 21.27 trillion dollars, and — the genuinely notable change — its primary income balance flipped from surplus to deficit in the first quarter, which attacks the exorbitant-privilege mechanism that finances the deficit on favourable terms. The bilateral resolution is concentration and financeability, not size: the base economy has a single dominant customer growing below its own target, an export basket a third of which is one commodity whose price is falling, and no reserve status, invoicing share or central bank swap line to fall back on, whereas the quote currency invoices roughly 40 to 50 per cent of global trade. The genuine counterweight, and the reason confidence sits at 52, is that the Reserve Bank's own September Statement cited resilient trading-partner demand and strong export prices supporting income growth — a direct contradiction of the falling terms-of-trade narrative from the institution with the best view of it.

Tactically the evidence is one bad trade print and two scheduled releases against a four-auction dairy recovery, which caps confidence. Strategically the same figures compound: balance-of-payments flows accumulate, and six months of a 3.6 per cent-of-GDP deficit funded from abroad by an economy with a single dominant customer is a real constraint where four weeks of it is not.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: New Zealand — dairy is roughly 30% of merchandise exports (GlobalDairyTrade index and whole milk powder the reference prices), plus meat, forestry and horticulture; a net energy importer, so higher oil is a terms-of-trade negative. Dairy up is strongly positive for the base currency; oil up is mildly negative.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: United States — now a net energy exporter, so higher oil is a mild terms-of-trade positive; no meaningful agricultural-soft exposure comparable to dairy; the dominant commodity channel runs through inflation rather than through the trade account, where higher energy prices reinforce the hawkish policy case.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Netting across the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Oil up 10%: base currency mildly negative as a net energy importer with a worsening terms of trade, quote currency mildly positive as a net energy exporter, and the second-order inflation channel is also quote-positive because higher energy prices reinforce the case for a Federal Reserve increase. Both legs therefore push the same way and the net effect is that the pair falls. Oil down 10%: base terms of trade improves and the quote loses its export benefit, which is pair-positive at first pass, but the same move removes the 27.5% petrol contribution to base headline inflation and with it the justification for further base-leg tightening, so the rates channel offsets most of the trade channel and the net is close to flat with a mild negative tilt. Dairy up: unambiguously pair-positive, because the base leg gains roughly 30% of its export basket while the quote leg is unaffected. Netting across the actual current configuration — Brent roughly 12% off its July high and the ANZ dairy sub-index down 11.3% year on year — the two moves have offset each other in the base economy's terms of trade while leaving the base leg's dominant export price falling, which is the net negative for the pair.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Pair falls. Base mildly negative, quote mildly positive, inflation channel quote-positive. Modestly bearish NZD/USD, with the caveat that sustained higher oil also keeps base-leg tradables inflation and therefore base-leg tightening alive, which partly offsets.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Pair roughly flat to modestly lower. The base terms of trade improves and the quote loses its energy-export benefit, which is pair-positive, but the same move accelerates base-leg disinflation by removing the petrol contribution to a 4.1% headline print, shortening the base-leg tightening cycle and offsetting the trade gain through the rates channel.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Dairy — the GlobalDairyTrade index and the whole milk powder average winning price. Roughly 30% of the base economy's merchandise exports, a fortnightly auction cadence, and no offsetting exposure on the quote side, which makes it the highest-frequency commodity input to any G10 pair and the only one that moves this pair asymmetrically.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Going into the window both central banks were more hawkish than their own curves, which is an unusual symmetry and would ordinarily cancel. It no longer cancels, because one of the two gaps has been resolved and the other has not. The Reserve Bank is the only G10 bank that publishes its own projected policy path, so its guidance gap is settled with a number rather than a hint, and on 2 September it published a path little changed from May — a fourth-quarter 2026 average OCR of 2.81 per cent against 2.84 per cent in May, consistent with a pause on 28 October and an increase to 3.00 per cent on 9 December, with the Committee stating that future decisions depend on its judgement of the balance of risks to medium-term inflation. That validated market pricing of roughly one further move and closed the 25 to 50 basis point hawkish gap the base dossier was relying on, without delivering the 3.5 per cent published peak one local bank had expected. The Federal Reserve's gap remains wide open in the opposite direction: the June Summary of Economic Projections carries a 2026 median of 3.8 per cent, which implies an increase outright, against futures pricing of 57 to 66 per cent, and the July meeting produced a 9-3 hold in which all three dissenters wanted to tighten — the first three-dissent meeting with a unified direction since September 2016. The sequencing compounds it: the base leg has now spoken and the quote leg speaks last, on 16 September, with a fresh projection round attached. Guidance is therefore asymmetrically against the pair for the remainder of the tactical window.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months guidance stops being a signal and becomes a test, and both banks face one on 9 December when the Reserve Bank publishes a new OCR track and the Federal Reserve a new Summary of Economic Projections on the same day. The base-leg test is whether the September path survives: the Committee revised 2027 inflation forecasts up on persistent domestic inflation with a majority seeing upside risks, which is materially more robust than the imported-and-fading framing the base dossier assumed and reduces the probability of a dovish December revision — that is the reason strategic confidence here is cut to 45 from the level a naive netting of the two dossiers would produce. Against it, the Bank's recent record is genuinely weak, with a May track superseded within six weeks by an off-track July increase and a September-quarter CPI peak revised from 4.3 to 3.3 per cent inside eight weeks, and it is publishing a rising OCR path alongside a CPI path that returns to 2 per cent by late 2027 while all Committee members see downside growth risks. The quote-leg test is the mirror image: the Federal Reserve's own 2027 median of 3.6 per cent makes any September increase terminal, so its December projections either confirm a reduction — pair-positive — or remove it, which would convert a terminal move into a cycle and be sharply pair-negative. The credibility differential is real but two-sided: the base bank is more transparent and resolves its guidance with a published number, while the quote bank carries an institutional independence question that its own analysts read as making a tightening more rather than less likely. Net, mildly against the pair at low confidence.

The Reserve Bank's upward revision to its 2027 inflation forecasts specifically weakens the strategic bearish case relative to what the base dossier assumed, and the confidence reduction is where that shows up.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The four weeks in front of the pair are unusually dense and unusually two-sided, which is why the honest stance is Neutral. The base-leg calendar is now largely behind the pair: the Statement landed on 2 September and the terms of trade plus the ANZ commodity index on 3 September, leaving the balance of payments on 16 September, second-quarter GDP on 17 September and the Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update on 29 September. The quote-leg calendar is all ahead and carries the bigger instruments: August payrolls on 4 September against a consensus of plus 58,000 after a print of minus 23,000, CPI on 11 September, the decision with projections on 16 September, and quarter-end dollar funding on 30 September. Asymmetric sensitivity cuts both ways and is the reason no direction can be assigned. Meanwhile the base-leg events are shallower but move the base currency further per unit of surprise given the lowest liquidity in the G10. Geopolitically, Middle East developments have been driving Brent and cut both ways for this pair: higher oil sustains the base economy's tradables inflation and therefore its tightening case while worsening its terms of trade, and mildly benefits the quote economy as a net energy exporter. A dense, symmetric calendar with an under-hedged options surface is a Neutral, not a lean.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The strategic event calendar is asymmetric in a way the tactical one is not, because it contains the base economy's three-year political cycle against a quote-economy election whose currency implications genuinely cancel. On the base side a general election is expected in November on the three-year parliamentary cycle, preceded by an independent Treasury Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update on 29 September that publishes the fiscal accounts into a campaign, and it lands in front of two of three rating agencies already carrying negative outlooks. Party positions differ materially on housing, immigration and fiscal policy, all three of which transmit directly to a currency in an economy of 5.3 million. On the quote side the 3 November midterms are two-sided by construction: a result constraining fiscal expansion is quote-positive through the deficit channel and quote-negative through growth, and the second-order effect on political pressure applied to a central bank that may have just tightened over presidential objection is unknowable in advance. Averaging one one-sided political risk against one genuinely ambiguous one leaves the factor pointing against the pair. Two further base-specific exposures reinforce it: roughly twelve fortnightly GlobalDairyTrade auctions fall inside the window, the highest-frequency commodity event affecting any G10 currency, and the base economy is earthquake-prone with a documented pattern of initial currency weakening on damage. None is individually likely; collectively they skew the distribution.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Neither sovereign moves this pair inside four weeks and the bilateral netting is close to exact, which makes this a considered Neutral rather than a placeholder. On levels the base sovereign is far stronger: net core Crown debt of 186.0 billion New Zealand dollars, or 41.3 per cent of GDP, in the eleven months to 31 May 2026, which is 2.8 billion better than the Budget forecast, with gross debt at 49.3 per cent, against quote-economy debt held by the public at 101 per cent of GDP and gross debt approaching 40 trillion dollars. On outlooks the ranking reverses: Moody's placed the base sovereign's Aaa on negative outlook on 22 April 2026 and Fitch moved its AA+ outlook to negative on 20 March, so two of three agencies are negative, while the quote sovereign carries Moody's Aa1, S&P AA+ and Fitch AA+ all with stable outlooks. On transmission the picture reverses again and this is the decisive point for four weeks: quote-economy fiscal deterioration is currently expressed as higher long-end yields — a 30-year at 5.22 per cent, a 20-year auction stopping at 5.204 against 5.163 per cent, a 30-year TIPS clearing 50 basis points higher — and in the present regime higher long yields are quote-currency-supportive, so the quote leg's fiscal problem is working backwards and is pair-negative rather than pair-positive. Base-economy auctions are clearing without stress at a ten-year yield of 4.74 per cent. Level favours the base, outlook favours the quote, transmission favours the quote, and no base-leg or quote-leg rating action is scheduled inside the window.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months both fiscal stories become live and they genuinely offset, which is why this remains Neutral at a reduced weight rather than being pressed into service for either side. The base-leg case is a trajectory and a calendar: Budget 2026 has net core Crown debt rising from 41.9 per cent of GDP in fiscal 2025 to a 46.1 per cent peak in fiscal 2028 with the return to surplus placed in fiscal 2029, and the 29 September Pre-election Update followed by a November election is the natural venue for that path to be marked to market in front of two agencies already on negative outlook. We would put an adverse base-leg rating action at roughly 10 to 15 per cent inside six months, and in a currency with 88,964 contracts of futures open interest and no domestic buyer of scale the transmission would be a gap rather than a drift. The quote-leg case is arithmetic that compounds automatically: projected interest costs of 1,039 billion dollars in fiscal 2026 would exceed the post-war high of 3.2 per cent of GDP, every quarter of low-coupon debt rolls into a 4.5 to 5.2 per cent curve, a deficit above 2 trillion dollars now drains bank reserves directly because the reverse repo facility is empty, and long-end auction reception is already deteriorating. If the quote central bank tightens on 16 September it worsens its own rollover cost, which is the specific interaction the market does not price. So the base leg faces a dated, low-probability, high-impact headline risk and the quote leg faces a certain, slow, self-inflicted deterioration whose current transmission channel is quote-supportive. Neither dominates and the honest bilateral answer is that they cancel.

Tactically nothing is scheduled on either leg and the quote leg's fiscal transmission is currently inverted. Strategically the base leg acquires a dated political and rating calendar while the quote leg's interest burden compounds automatically, and the two remain in balance because the base risk is low-probability and high-impact while the quote risk is certain and slow.

That skew is a real directional tell, but at minus 0.193 per cent the near tenor is mild and negative risk reversals are the resting state for a high-beta commodity currency against the reserve asset, so it is not enough to carry a stance on its own. strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the dollar funding channel is a persistent headwind for this pair on three separable mechanisms, none of which requires a forecast of crisis. First, the quantity of dollar liquidity is contracting at the margin: reserve balances are drifting toward the roughly 3 trillion dollar minimum comfortable level with the reverse repo buffer that absorbed three years of tightening now empty at 702 million, and bill supply from a deficit above 2 trillion dollars drains bank reserves directly rather than being intermediated by money funds. The December 2025 precedent is the template rather than an aberration — SOFR to interest-on-reserves spreads at their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiking to a record 74.6 billion dollars on 31 December before collapsing to zero in January — and the year-end turn falls inside this window. Tighter dollar funding moves the quote currency to the left-hand side of the dollar smile, which is unambiguously pair-negative. Second, the base leg is structurally short global dollar liquidity: it must import capital month after month to fund a 3.6 per cent-of-GDP current account deficit against a net international investment position of minus 42.8 per cent and net external debt of 49.0 per cent, and it does so without a Federal Reserve backstop. Third, even on a constructive base-leg path of reaching 3.00 per cent by 9 December, one quote-leg increase leaves the differential at roughly minus 87.5 basis points, so the funding cost of holding the pair long persists throughout. The genuine offset, and the reason confidence is 55 rather than higher, is institutional: the rebranding of the facility as standing repo operations with full allotment and no aggregate limit is a permanent backstop upgrade that caps the tail at pressure rather than crisis.

The reinforcing cluster is external and structural. The base economy runs a current account deficit of 3.6 per cent of GDP whose improvement stalled three quarters ago, on a primary income deficit of roughly 3.3 billion New Zealand dollars a quarter and a net international investment position of minus 42.8 per cent; dairy is roughly 30 per cent of merchandise exports with the ANZ sub-index down 11.3 per cent year on year and Fonterra having cut its farmgate midpoint from 9.75 to 9.25; the dominant customer printed second-quarter GDP of 4.3 per cent below its own target; and all of that must be funded continuously from abroad without a Federal Reserve swap line at exactly the point in the calendar when reserve balances are drifting toward 3 trillion dollars with the reverse repo buffer empty and the year-end funding turn approaching. Policy and Rates, the heaviest factor, is Neutral: the base bank still has an increase to deliver on 9 December while the quote bank's own 2027 median of 3.6 per cent makes its next move a reduction, so the differential narrows on the direction of travel even as it stays punishing in level. consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast_source: BNZ Research, BNP Paribas Wealth Management, ANZ, Westpac New Zealand, MUFG and ING bank research desks; an aggregator forecast (0.58660 Sep-26 / 0.59560 Dec-26 / 0.60470 Mar-27) is flagged separately as a non-bank extrapolation site and is not treated as a survey median
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bearish to 0.5750 at the 3-6 month mark
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Roughly 150 pips below the bank cluster's 0.60 centre and below MUFG's 0.5900 low at the strategic horizon; inside the lower half of BNZ's 0.56-0.60 range rather than at its midpoint
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three things, and only the first is a forecast. First, timing of information: almost every level in the cluster was set between 13 and 27 August, before the 2 September Statement published a track essentially unchanged from May and before the quote leg's projection round became the only open guidance gap. Second, weighting: we put External Balance at 0.16 strategically and read it bilaterally rather than in isolation, so a base economy with a stalled 3.6 per cent-of-GDP deficit, a third of its exports in one commodity down 11.3 per cent year on year, and a dominant customer growing below target is a different object from a quote economy whose deficit is larger in absolute terms but financed in its own reserve currency with a 40 to 50 per cent global invoicing share. Third, funding: no bank level we can source appears conditioned on reserve balances at 2,916 billion dollars with an empty reverse repo buffer heading into a year-end turn, which is the specific mechanism that moved the dollar in December 2025 without moving the policy rate.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: The pair breaks the two-touch shelf and settles in the 0.57241-0.57456 zone, delivering roughly 132 pips of spot plus roughly 19 pips of accrued carry over four months against a consensus that has it flat to 120 pips higher — a 250 to 300 pip divergence realised. The gated surface makes it cheap to hold: nothing in the term structure at 7.955/8.266/8.414 per cent charges for the events that would deliver it.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: The specific way this is wrong is a Federal Reserve hold on 16 September, which strands a pair-short crowded on both legs and squeezes the pair through the six-touch band toward 0.5940 within a week. Odds have already moved that way, to nearly 50.2 per cent from 63.2 per cent. The strategic version is worse and slower: a base bank that delivers 3.00 per cent in December on genuinely persistent domestic inflation while the quote bank's projections confirm a 2027 reduction would compress the differential toward minus 60 basis points and invert Factors 1, 6 and 10 together — at which point consensus at 0.60 is right and a short entered at 0.58818 loses 118 pips plus nothing in carry, since the roll still pays the short.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons agree in sign and almost in magnitude, but they are built from different materials and that distinction matters more than the agreement. The tactical score is concentrated: Policy and Rates and Inflation and Growth contribute minus 0.2346 of the minus 0.3126 between them, and both resolve on dated events inside the window. The strategic score is almost pure breadth: the heaviest factor is explicitly Neutral, seven factors lean mildly against the pair, none with a confidence above 55, and the largest single contributor is the external accounts at minus 0.0832. So the same direction is being expressed by the rates and funding channels over four weeks and by the external, guidance, funding and political channels over six months, with the rates channel handing off to the balance of payments as the weight schedule shifts External Balance from 0.06 to 0.16.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: No stance reversal to navigate. What there is instead is a handover, and the handover date is the second half of October: the base economy's September-quarter CPI, then the 28 October simultaneous decisions, culminating on 9 December when a new base OCR track and a quote SEP land the same day.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Because the stances agree, the tactical position can legitimately be the opening leg of the strategic one rather than a trade with an expiry — but the two rest on different evidence and must be monitored against different signposts. The tactical view lives or dies on 16 September and can be judged within ninety minutes of the statement; the strategic view lives or dies on the base economy's external accounts and on 9 December. Practically: enter the tactical short on strength into 0.5885-0.5910 with a stop above 0.5945 at half size, and if 16 September delivers, roll the stop out to 0.6000 and hold the residual as the strategic position rather than re-entering. The one configuration that breaks both at once is a quote-leg hold on 16 September followed by a base leg that delivers to 3.00 per cent in December on persistent domestic inflation.

catalysts.event: RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement, OCR decision and republished OCR track (delivered: 25bp increase to 2.75%, track little changed from May)
catalysts.rationale: The base leg's only high-information event inside the tactical window, and it resolved without the hawkish surprise the base dossier's bullish case required. The published Q4 2026 average OCR of 2.81 per cent against 2.84 in May implies a pause on 28 October and an increase to 3.00 per cent on 9 December, ratifying rather than beating market pricing of roughly one further move. The differential narrows mechanically to minus 87.5 basis points, but the guidance gap closes and the positioning squeeze loses its trigger. The pair traded a 106-pip range and closed down 40 pips on the day.

catalysts.event: Statistics New Zealand Overseas Trade Indexes (June quarter) and ANZ World Commodity Price Index for August
catalysts.rationale: Two base-leg commodity releases on the same day, one after the Statement, following a March-quarter terms of trade decline of 2.0 per cent and a July commodity index fall of 3.9 per cent in world terms with dairy down 6.5 per cent on the month. Transmission is direct because dairy is roughly 30 per cent of base merchandise exports and there is no offsetting exposure on the quote side. Outcomes not known to this analysis.

catalysts.event: United States August non-farm payrolls, unemployment rate and average hourly earnings
catalysts.rationale: The largest two-sided event inside the window and the single largest risk to the tactical bearish case. Consensus is plus 58,000 after a July print of minus 23,000, with average hourly earnings at a five-year low of 3.2 per cent. A second consecutive contraction would make a 16 September increase very difficult to defend, remove the quote leg's unpriced upside and invert the tactical case inside a week; a firm print does the opposite. Odds were already nearly 50.2 per cent, down from 63.2 per cent going into it.

The last quote-leg inflation print before the decision, against a July base of 3.4 per cent headline and 2.5 per cent core. The bilateral subtlety is that quote core CPI sits 80 basis points below quote core PCE, an inversion of the usual relationship, and the Federal Reserve targets PCE — so a soft core CPI print is less pair-positive than it appears. Transmission runs entirely through the quote leg's front end.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The dominant event for the pair now that the base leg has spoken. A 25 basis point increase was priced at roughly 57 to 66 per cent in futures against roughly 48 to 55 per cent in prediction markets and a June median of 3.8 per cent that implies one outright, though that gap has narrowed since Waller's remarks. Delivery restores the differential to minus 112.5 basis points against a base front end just told to expect nothing until December, and hits a base currency with no Federal Reserve swap line through both the rate and the funding channel. The pair's own term structure is in contango into it.

catalysts.event: Statistics New Zealand Balance of Payments and International Investment Position, June quarter
catalysts.rationale: The base leg's heaviest strategic factor gets its quarterly update on the same day as the quote leg's decision. The annual current account deficit has been effectively flat for three quarters at roughly 3.6 per cent of GDP and the July merchandise trade balance printed minus 1.95 billion New Zealand dollars against an expectation nearer minus 175 million, so the June-quarter accounts are more likely to confirm the stall than the improvement. Transmission is through financeability rather than trade settlement, since bilateral goods trade with the quote economy is only about 10.4 billion dollars two-way.

catalysts.event: Statistics New Zealand Gross Domestic Product, June quarter
catalysts.rationale: The bilateral growth differential is the base economy at 1.47 per cent year on year against the quote at 2.10 per cent, and this print is the first hard test of whether the Reserve Bank is right that activity will strengthen and broaden. Survey evidence points above the 0.8 per cent March-quarter run rate while retail volumes and a decade-high 5.6 per cent unemployment point below it, so the print is genuinely two-sided for the pair.

catalysts.event: New Zealand Treasury Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update
catalysts.rationale: An independent Treasury view of the base economy's fiscal accounts published into an election campaign, against a Budget 2026 path that has net core Crown debt rising to a 46.1 per cent-of-GDP peak in fiscal 2028, and landing in front of two of three agencies already on negative outlook. The bilateral asymmetry is transmission rather than level: base debt at 41.3 per cent of GDP is far below the quote's 101 per cent, but a base rating headline gaps a currency with only 88,964 contracts of futures open interest. Note the offsetting fact that the bond programme was cut NZ$6 billion across the forecast period at Budget 2026.

catalysts.event: September quarter-end United States dollar funding date
catalysts.rationale: The first quarter-end since quote-leg reserve balances resumed falling, at 2,916 billion dollars and heading toward the roughly 3 trillion minimum, with the overnight reverse repo facility drained to 702 million from a 2.55 trillion peak. Tighter dollar funding moves the quote currency to the left-hand side of the dollar smile, which is directly pair-negative, and the base leg must fund a 3.6 per cent-of-GDP external deficit continuously without a Federal Reserve backstop — partly in dollars, through a minimum US$3 billion ECP programme. A cross-currency basis of minus 0.81 basis points says nobody is hedging it.

catalysts.event: Statistics New Zealand Consumers Price Index, September quarter (indicative date)
catalysts.rationale: The first base-leg print in which the petrol base effect substantially unwinds — petrol contributed 23.5 per cent of the annual rise to 4.1 per cent and Brent has fallen roughly 12 per cent from its July high — against a Reserve Bank near-term peak already revised to 3.3 per cent. Scored Ambiguous rather than Bearish because the September Statement revised 2027 inflation forecasts up on persistent domestic inflation, so a soft print confirms the fading-overshoot thesis while a firm core reading validates a December increase and is pair-positive. Date indicative, not confirmed in this analysis.

catalysts.event: RBNZ Monetary Policy Review and Federal Open Market Committee decision — both banks decide on the same day
catalysts.rationale: The first of two simultaneous decision dates, and the asymmetry is structural: the base leg publishes no new OCR track at a Review and has already signalled a pause, so it can only surprise through framing, while the quote leg meets without projections at the first opportunity to judge whether a September increase was terminal. One leg with a pre-committed pause against one leg with an open question tilts the day against the pair.

Genuinely two-sided by construction. A result constraining fiscal expansion is quote-positive through the deficit channel and quote-negative through growth; a result enabling it is the reverse; and the second-order effect on political pressure applied to a central bank that may have just tightened over presidential objection cannot be signed in advance. No premium for it exists anywhere on the pair's gated volatility surface at 8.414 per cent for 185.7 days.

Confirmed for 7 November 2026 by Prime Minister Luxon on 21 January 2026, four days after the quote economy's midterms — so the two political events land inside a single week and neither is priced. Base parties differ materially on housing, immigration and fiscal policy, all three of which transmit directly to a currency in an economy of 5.3 million, and the outcome looks genuinely uncertain: the 13-17 June 1 News-Verian poll showed 29 against 32 for the two largest parties. Scored Ambiguous because the direction of any result is unknowable in advance, but the clustering with the quote-leg election is a volatility event the surface does not charge for.

catalysts.event: RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement with a new published OCR track and FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections — both on the same day
catalysts.rationale: The single largest bilateral repricing event in the strategic window, because both legs publish a full projection round within hours of each other. The base leg is signalled to raise to 3.00 per cent and either confirms or revises the September path; the quote leg either retains its 2027 median of 3.6 per cent, which makes any September increase terminal and is pair-positive, or removes it, which converts a terminal move into a cycle and is sharply pair-negative. The two outcomes can compound in either direction, which is why this is Ambiguous despite a bearish strategic verdict.

catalysts.event: Year-end United States dollar funding turn
catalysts.rationale: The direct analogue of December 2025, when SOFR-to-interest-on-reserves spreads reached their widest since 2020 and standing repo usage spiked to a record 74.6 billion dollars on 31 December before collapsing to zero in January. Every precondition is in place and several are worse, though full-allotment standing repo operations should cap the tail at pressure rather than crisis. Tighter dollar funding is pair-negative through the base leg's continuous external funding need.

invalidators.condition: The FOMC holds the target range at 3.50-3.75% on 16 September rather than raising it
invalidators.mechanism: The pair-short is crowded on both legs simultaneously — 31,994 contracts short the base against only 88,964 of open interest, plus 18,682 long the quote — and a hold strands it in a market with documented gapping behaviour and no domestic buyer of scale on the base side; the covering would be transmitted through this pair rather than through the Dollar Index.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Fed funds futures-implied probability and the FOMC statement, against a 0.59413 close on the pair
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Daily until 16 September, then at the statement

invalidators.condition: NZD/USD closes above 0.59865, the 200-week average, on four consecutive weekly closes
invalidators.mechanism: A pair that has been unable to close above its own four-year mean for 28 weeks reclaiming it durably would trigger systematic trend-following flow in a market too small to absorb it, and would invalidate the structural component of the bearish case irrespective of the fundamental factors.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Weekly close versus the 200-week simple moving average of trading-day closes

invalidators.condition: The base-leg September-quarter CPI prints at or above 4.1% with the sectoral factor model rising above 3.0% from its four-quarter plateau of 2.7%
invalidators.mechanism: It would establish the base economy's inflation as domestic and persistent rather than an imported fuel shock, validate a full base-leg tightening cycle to 3.50% rather than the pause-then-one-more path the September track implies, and compress the NZ-US two-year deficit from roughly 73 basis points toward zero. The Reserve Bank's own upward revision to its 2027 inflation forecasts makes this less remote than the base dossier assumed.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: Statistics New Zealand headline CPI and the RBNZ sectoral factor model in the M1 release
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Quarterly, next in the third week of October

invalidators.condition: The three-month cross-currency basis moves beyond minus 30bp for three consecutive sessions from minus 0.81 today
invalidators.new_stance: Keeps the stance Bearish but invalidates the framework
invalidators.mechanism: The pair would then be falling for funding rather than rate reasons — the quote currency moving from the right-hand exceptionalism side of the dollar smile to the left-hand stress side — at which point the base leg's absent swap line and 3.6%-of-GDP external deficit dominate and the rate-differential lens stops being the right one, with far larger and faster moves than the scenario levels here allow.

invalidators.condition: Leveraged funds move from a net short of 31,994 base-leg contracts to net long while NZD/USD fails to close above 0.59413
invalidators.mechanism: The mechanical support that has quietly limited declines all year would be exhausted while the pair remained capped by its most-transacted band — leaving it with negative carry, a stalled current account and no positioning cushion. This invalidates the single Bullish factor in the tactical table rather than the direction.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: CFTC Traders in Financial Futures leveraged-fund net contracts, cross-checked against the legacy non-commercial series
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Weekly, Friday for the preceding Tuesday

invalidators.condition: GlobalDairyTrade index rises more than 10% cumulatively across three consecutive auctions with whole milk powder above 4,000 US dollars a tonne, prompting Fonterra to restore its 2026/27 forecast toward the 9.75 opening midpoint
invalidators.mechanism: External Balance is the heaviest strategic contributor at minus 0.0832 on a 0.16 weight and its evidence base is the dairy complex being down 11.3% year on year; reversing that alone takes the strategic score from minus 0.3254 toward minus 0.24 and the conviction to 2.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: GDT index and whole milk powder average winning price; Fonterra farmgate announcements
invalidators.monitor_frequency: Fortnightly for GDT, ad hoc for Fonterra

invalidators.condition: The 9 December FOMC projection round removes the implied 2027 reduction by lifting the 2027 median above 3.6% while the base-leg track published the same day is revised down
invalidators.new_stance: Strategically Bearish with conviction 4 and a target of 0.5700 or below
invalidators.mechanism: The two projection rounds would compound rather than offset — converting a terminal quote-leg increase into a cycle at the same moment the base leg admits its own path was too steep. This strengthens rather than reverses the thesis and is listed because it is the specific configuration that would justify adding.
invalidators.monitor_indicator: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections 2027 median and the RBNZ published OCR track

signposts.invalidates_if: Falls below 35% without an offsetting hawkish base-leg surprise

Watching the policy rates alone would miss that, and watching the ten-year differential is useless here — both legs in the payload are monthly June vintages showing minus 1 basis point.

signposts.current_level: 3,585 US dollars a tonne after four consecutive positive index auctions, still below the 3,706 of 2 June; index plus 0.9% at Event 411 on 1 September

Roughly twelve auctions fall inside the strategic window.

The monotonic steepening is the single most direct statement of where protection is being bought, and it is concentrated at the tenor covering the 7 November election and the 9 December double policy event.

signposts.current_level: Minus 31,994 contracts on the Traders in Financial Futures basis for the 25 August report date against total open interest of 88,964, with the legacy non-commercial series showing minus 14,200 for the same date and wire reporting of the legacy series citing minus 50.0 thousand in late July
signposts.confirms_if: The short holds above 30,000 contracts while spot fails at 0.58837 — selling that is fundamental rather than speculative

It must be read alongside Dollar Index non-commercial length at 18,682 contracts, four weeks off a three-and-a-half-year high — a base-leg short being covered while quote-leg length is also being cut is a very different signal from either in isolation.

signposts.current_level: Not established in this analysis; the series is published but no level is asserted here
signposts.confirms_if: The non-resident share falls materially through the pre-election and election window
signposts.invalidates_if: The share rises through the 29 September fiscal update and the 7 November election, indicating foreign capital is being attracted rather than repelled by the base leg's fiscal and political calendar

Bilateral goods trade of only about 10.4 billion dollars two-way is immaterial by comparison; the capital account is where this pair is decided. The quote leg has no equivalent vulnerability because it borrows in its own reserve currency.

assumptions: The payload delivered 130 weekday bars covering 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, with spot 0.58818 at spotDate 2026-09-03; moving averages, support/resistance zones and the 200-week figure are computed over the whole stored history of 4,879 weekday bars back to 2007-12-24, not over the 130 bars shown.

There is a two-session gap between spotDate (2026-09-03) and the stated VALUATION_DATE (2026-09-01); every level, target and pip calculation is anchored to the payload spot of 0.58818 and no fresher web quote has been substituted. The payload spot already reflects the 2 September RBNZ decision while the gated rate block's base policy rate of 2.50% is dated pre-decision (28 August); both the pre-decision -112.5bp and post-decision -87.5bp differentials are stated wherever relevant.

The direction verdict's effective information cutoff is 2026-09-04, incorporating the delivered RBNZ outcome; this pass extends that to include Governor Waller's 4 September remarks and the resulting fall in Fed hike odds to roughly 50.2%, disclosed in the rationale rather than used to re-score any factor.

The 52-week intraday high of 1.71632 and its associated percentile of 3 are a data-quality artefact from a single bad tick on the 29 April 2026 bar and are not used anywhere in this report; all range discussion uses the closing basis (52w high 0.60657, low 0.55947, percentile 61).

The 200-week moving average (0.59865) is treated as a first-class structural reference; its slope of minus 0.00006/week means it cannot converge on a static spot within any tradable timescale, so the setup resolves only through price, not through the average's drift.

pair_3m_iv (8.266%) is measured at 94.7 days rather than 90 because CME lists quarterly futures/options (6N/6NZ6); no implied-volatility percentile is asserted because the surface has no stored history from which to compute one.

Forward points are derived from the gated futures roll premium (+94.9bp annualised, 13.6-to-104.7-day legs) applied to payload spot rather than read from a live vendor forwards screen, which moved materially within 35 minutes in both standalone dossiers' testing; by covered interest parity the roll premium embeds both the interest differential and the cross-currency basis, which cannot be separated without an OIS curve, so the implied basis (~-18 to -27bp) is labelled a derivation, not a quote.
Both legs' 10-year yields in the payload are monthly IRLTLT01 observations dated 2026-06-01 and are used only to state a vintage differential, never as live levels.

Bilateral trade figures are taken verbatim from the injected IMF DOTS 2024 block; the two partners' reported directions differ as DOTS data normally does, and both are stated rather than averaged; two-way goods trade of roughly 10.4bn dollars is treated as immaterial against either economy.

Positioning carries an explicit reliability caveat: three CFTC-related series disagree on the base leg's level (TFF -31,994; legacy non-commercial -14,200; wire reporting of the legacy series near -50,000 in late July); direction is clear, level is not, and this caps Factor 4 confidence below 50 at both horizons.

Weight adjustments (four tactical, two strategic, each within ±0.05) are carried verbatim from the direction verdict and were not modified in this pass; all ten applied weights sum to exactly 1.00 at each horizon.

The ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, weighted contributions, net scores and rationales are carried verbatim from the settled direction verdict, which scored them without access to the price payload; Factor 9's structural half was completed from the payload in this pass and corroborates rather than changes the stances as issued.

The New Zealand general election date (7 November 2026) was not asserted by the original verdict and was established in this pass from a secondary source reporting the Prime Minister's 21 January 2026 announcement; it is used in the catalyst list and signposts but not to alter any factor stance.
